teaser.text: Haier Smart Home is a global seller of household appliances, connected-home solutions, and commercial cooling systems. Its money comes in through products, projects, and distribution, then goes out through the costs of making, selling, delivering, and supporting them.

stock.title: Haier Smart Home stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Haier Smart Home stock forecast: weighted scenarios, cash generation, risks and valuation in plain English.
stock.opening: Haier Smart Home's weighted case points to HKD21.78 in October 2027 and HKD25.98 in October 2029. Haier Smart Home's outcome hinges on whether HVAC growth and localized factories restore earnings and cash without sacrificing the dividend.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Haier Smart Home makes money, compares with its rivals, is managed, and faces its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Haier Smart Home's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is HKD21.78 in October 2027. Including dividends, that is a 15% return from today’s HKD20.12. The weighted price reaches HKD23.67 in October 2028, a 31% return including dividends. By October 2029, it reaches HKD25.98, a 50% return.
The last-date range runs from HKD13.41 in the bear case to HKD43.59 in the bull case. The bear has 30% probability, the base 52%, and the bull 18%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Haier Smart Home's stock forecast?

paragraphs.text: The bear case falls from CNY16,500 million to CNY15,300 million as weak replacement demand, tariffs and underused factories compress margins. The bull case rises from CNY21,000 million to CNY25,500 million, requiring recovery, profitable share gains and better HVAC utilization. H1 2026 net income fell to CNY10,316 million, while Smart HVAC revenue rose 6.1% and segment profit rose 26.8%; that contrast supports recovery potential but also argues against making the bull case central.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Haier Smart Home really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash is not yet money available for every purpose. Haier still has to maintain factories and equipment, pay leases and interest, and fund the business’s future. Its real free-cash-flow measure also deducts share-based pay because issuing shares can dilute existing owners even when no cash leaves immediately.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Haier Smart Home today?

paragraphs.text: A price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, compares the share price with profit per share. A trailing P/E uses the last twelve months of profit, while a forward P/E uses an estimate of future profit. The forward multiple is lower when investors expect earnings to recover, so it is a bet rather than a description of what Haier has already earned. That matters because profit attributable to shareholders fell 14.3% in H1 2026.

blocks.heading: Is Haier Smart Home's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, dividends and share repurchases together took almost all of free cash flow. That can be a deliberate choice when management believes the shares offer better value than another acquisition. It also leaves less internally generated cash for factories, purchases and unexpected shocks. If distributions exceed free cash flow, the difference must come from existing cash, investments or borrowing.

blocks.heading: What could change Haier Smart Home's dividend?

paragraphs.text: Management promises a minimum cash dividend payout ratio of 58% for 2026 and at least 60% for 2027 and 2028. No interim dividend was recommended for H1 2026. The forecast assigns bear, base and bull probabilities of 30%/52%/18%. The bear case reflects weak replacement demand, tariffs and underused factories; the bull requires profitable share gains, stronger HVAC utilization and better cash generation.

From 2028 onward, cash conversion will decide whether Haier can fund dividends and buybacks together. Renewed repurchases alongside stable investment would support the base-to-bull shift; stopped buybacks, weaker free cash flow and subdued margins would move the forecast toward the bear case.

blocks.heading: What has Haier Smart Home guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Haier has also promised a specific shareholder return. It said the cash dividend payout ratio would be at least 58% in 2026. It set at least 60% for the following two years. A payout ratio is the share of attributable profit distributed as dividends, not a return of that percentage on the share price. Because Haier did not recommend an interim dividend for the first half of 2026, the full-year distribution will be the important test.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Haier Smart Home's next results?

paragraphs.text: Two factory milestones are close. Investors should watch for the Thailand washing-machine groundbreaking on October 26 and the opening of the second phase of the refrigerator and freezer complex in Egypt in mid-to-late November. A ceremony is only an early signal. The meaningful evidence will be on-time production, rising volume and enough customer demand to justify the fixed costs.

The verdict will come from margins, factory utilization and operating cash flow. If those improve as capacity expands, Haier may be able to fund both its promised shareholder returns and its next phase of growth.
